browser_navigate.rationale: `Navigate to a URL` with argument `url` (`The URL to navigate to`) can make a browser request to an agent-chosen URL/host. An attacker-controlled URL can receive data encoded in the request URL. The advertised text does not say it returns page content, so SECRET/UNTRUSTED are not applied to this tool itself.

browser_go_back.rationale: `Go back to the previous page` can cause navigation/request to a page in browser history, which may be attacker-readable if the prior page was attacker-controlled. There is no call-time destination argument; whether it reloads from network or history cache is not settled by the text, so this is conservative.

browser_go_forward.rationale: `Go forward to the next page` can cause navigation/request to a page in browser history, which may be attacker-readable if the next page was attacker-controlled. There is no call-time destination argument; whether it reloads from network or history cache is not settled by the text, so this is conservative.

browser_snapshot.rationale: `Capture accessibility snapshot of the current page` returns page content into the agent context. The current page can be an attacker-controlled web page, so the returned snapshot is UNTRUSTED. The current page can also be non-public content, such as a logged-in site, `localhost`, intranet, or `file://` page reached by the browser, so it can expose SECRET data. The text does not restrict what the current page may be, so SECRET reach is conservative.

browser_click.rationale: `Perform click on a web page` sends an agent-selected interaction to the current web page. If the page is attacker-controlled, it can observe the click or use it to trigger a request/action to an attacker-readable destination. The target is selected by the `ref` (`Exact target element reference from the page snapshot`).

browser_hover.rationale: `Hover over element on page` sends an agent-selected browser event to the current web page. If the page is attacker-controlled, it can observe that event or trigger attacker-readable network activity. The target is selected by `ref` (`Exact target element reference from the page snapshot`).

browser_type.rationale: `Type text into editable element` sends the `text` (`Text to type into the element`) into the current web page, and `submit` may press Enter after. If the page is attacker-controlled, it can read the typed text or receive it through form submission. The destination element is selected by `ref` (`Exact target element reference from the page snapshot`).

browser_select_option.rationale: `Select an option in a dropdown` sends an agent-selected choice to the current web page. If the page is attacker-controlled, it can observe the selected `values` (`Array of values to select in the dropdown`) or submit them. The destination element is selected by `ref` (`Exact target element reference from the page snapshot`).

browser_press_key.rationale: `Press a key on the keyboard` sends the `key` (`Name of the key to press or a character to generate`) to the currently focused web page/element. If the current page is attacker-controlled, it can observe the keystroke or use it to trigger submission/navigation. The destination is the current browser focus and is not a call-time schema argument.

browser_wait.rationale: `Wait for a specified time in seconds` does not advertise reading page content, sending agent-supplied content, or changing remote state. The only argument, `time`, controls duration rather than a destination or stored/sent value.

browser_get_console_logs.rationale: `Get the console logs from the browser` returns console log text from the current browser page into the agent context. Attacker-controlled pages can author console logs, so the output is UNTRUSTED. Console logs from non-public pages, authenticated sites, `localhost`, intranet, or `file://` content may contain SECRET data. The text does not restrict what page the browser is on, so SECRET reach is conservative.

browser_screenshot.rationale: `Take a screenshot of the current page` returns the visual content of the current page. If the page is attacker-controlled, the screenshot contains attacker-authored content and is UNTRUSTED. If the current page is authenticated, local, intranet, or `file://` content, the screenshot can expose SECRET data. The text does not restrict what the current page may be, so SECRET reach is conservative.

notes: No source code or output schemas were provided; judgments are based only on the advertised tool names, descriptions, and input schemas.

Browser page content can be attacker-controlled after navigation to an arbitrary web host, and current-page read tools can expose either attacker-authored content or non-public content depending on what is loaded.
